t.E101.agn: In 2013 EFSA did not set an ADI because long-term and reproductive studies were lacking; however, it concluded that it was unlikely to raise a safety concern at the current authorised uses and levels. In 1981 JECFA had set a group ADI of 0–0.5 mg/kg body weight/day for riboflavin and riboflavin-5'-phosphate.
t.E101.body: The phosphate form is rapidly converted to free riboflavin in the gut and is processed through normal metabolic pathways.
t.E101.found.0: In the EU, as a Group II colour, in many foods at quantum satis: flavoured fermented milk products and cheeses, confectionery and chewing gum, breakfast cereals, fine bakery wares, sauces, mustard and seasonings, flavoured drinks, cider and fruit wines, snacks
t.E101.found.1: Canned red fruit and canned vegetables (excluding olives)
t.E101.found.3: Fish and crustacean pastes, smoked fish
t.E101.found.5: Aromatised wines (americano, bitter vino; up to 100 mg/l)
t.E101.prod: Riboflavin can be produced by fermentation or by chemical synthesis; the phosphate form is obtained by chemical treatment.
t.E101.regx.0: Re-evaluated; no ADI set, safety concern unlikely at authorised uses.
t.E101.regx.1: Group ADI of 0–0.5 mg/kg body weight for riboflavin and riboflavin-5'-phosphate.
t.E101.regx.2: Group II colour: quantum satis in the permitted food categories.
t.E101.summary: Vitamin B2; yellow-orange in colour. It is used both as a vitamin supplement and as a colour.
t.E101.what: A colour that gives a yellow-orange colour; it consists of vitamin B2 (riboflavin) and its phosphate form.
